newsitem.title: USA: Strengthening winds lift Bill to hurricane status.
newsitem.headline: Strengthening winds lift Bill to hurricane status.

text.p: Tropical Storm Bill was upgraded to hurricane status on Saturday after passing well west of Bermuda, U.S. forecasters said.

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), Bill, the second named storm of the 1997 Atlantic season, was located at latitude 38.6 north, longitude 60.2 west, or about 660 miles (1,056 km) south-southwest of Newfoundland.
"Bill has developed an eye and reached hurricane status," a forecaster at the National Hurricane Center said.
Bill's winds had reached 75 mph (120 kph) and was moving northeasterly at 26 mph (42 kph), a direction the hurricane was likely to sustain through late Sunday morning, forecasters said.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph). Hurricanes form when winds top 74 mph (118 kph).
The first tropical storm of the season, Ana, formed on July 1 off the North Carolina coast but bypassed Bermuda and faded as it moved northeast in the Atlantic without touching land.
